the hardest-to-reverse\ndecision is drafted in `docs/adr/ADR-006-login-limiter-in-memory.md`.\n\n## Decisions\n\n**S2 Login hardening**\n- Ordinary failed logins stay 401 + `LOGIN_ERROR` (pinned by `tests/test_t01_login.py`).\n- A locked-out attempt: status 429, the login page re-rendered with its own lockout message.\n- Lockout: 5 failed logins for one email within 15 minutes; refused even with the right password.\n- Keyed on the typed email (trimmed, lowercased), unknown and deactivated emails included.\n- A successful login (before lockout) clears that email's failures.\n- One module-level limiter in memory; `clock` attribute, `time.monotonic` by default.\n- Fixture: `reset_limiter` in `tests/conftest.py`, autouse; clears failures, restores the real clock.\n\n**F8 Switchable theme**\n- Themes: `app/themes/classic/style.css` (today's `publish.CSS`, moved) and\n  `app/themes/kenyon/style.css` (light only, Kenyon purple header bar and links, serif headings,\n  same layout rules: no horizontal overflow at 390 px).\n- `settings` table of key/value rows: `key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL`; theme is `('theme', '<name>')`.\n  Only a folder that exists under `app/themes/` is accepted.\n- Fallback when no row: `CMS_THEME`, default `classic`; `.env.example` gets `CMS_THEME=classic`.\n- Saving a theme is a site update (`update_site`): no wifi means the change is refused.\n- The console preview's `/style.css` serves the selected theme too.\n- Settings link in `templates/admin/_nav.html`: inside the `account.is_admin` block. `/admin/settings` guarded by `require_admin`.\n\n**S1 Access matrix**\n- Routes: `create_app().routes` whose dependency tree contains `require_admin`.\n- Path parameters: real ids. The test seeds demo content; `{item_id}` = a real page's id,\n  `{account_id}` = the editor's id.\n- Anonymous: `follow_redirects=False`, status in (302, 303, 307), Location path `/login`.\n- Editor: 403 or a redirect. POSTs carry a valid session CSRF token, so a 403 can only come from `require_admin`.\n\n## Session checklist\n\nBefore each: `git switch main && git pull`, then the two checks at the end (runbook 8):\n`uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` (22/22) and `uv run pytest -q` (212 + new, all passed).\n\n### 1. S2 Login hardening\n- Phase: `echo S2 > .claude/state/phase`\n- Issue/branch: none; on `main`.\n- Prompt 1 (`/clear` first):\n  `/tdd Make a wrong password and an unknown email produce the same login error message and status code. Add tests/test_login_hardening.py with a test that asserts both responses match.`\n- Prompt 2 (`/clear` first):\n  `/tdd Rate-limit login, keyed on the account: after 5 failed attempts for one email within 15 minutes, refuse further attempts for that email with 429 and the login page showing a lockout message, even with the right password. Count failures by the typed email, trimmed and lowercased, including emails with no account or a deactivated one. A successful login clears that email's failures. Keep failures in one module-level limiter in memory with a clock attribute (time.monotonic by default) so tests can freeze and advance it. Ordinary failures stay 401 with LOGIN_ERROR. In tests/test_login_hardening.py, test that attempt 6 is refused, that a login works again once 15 minutes have passed, and that another email can still log in from the same client. Add an autouse fixture reset_limiter to tests/conftest.py that clears the limiter and restores the real clock; change nothing else in conftest. No new dependencies. See docs/adr/ADR-006-login-limiter-in-memory.md.`\n- Review: `/code-review`; fix findings.\n- Commit: `S2: ...`, push. Stage only S2 files (leave CONTEXT.md and ADR-006 for P3).\n- Report row: `| S2 | tests/test_login_hardening.py; fixture reset_limiter in tests/conftest.py |`\n\n### 2. F8 Switchable theme, through P1\n- Issue first: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus F8: Switchable theme\"`; body = F8's\n  acceptance table word for word, then `Blocked by: none` (`gh label create stretch` if missing).\n- Phase: `echo T<N> > .claude/state/phase`\n- Branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c mp2plus-theme`\n- Prompt (`/clear` first): the manual's F8 prompt with `#N`, plus:\n  `The two themes are classic (today's CSS, moved unchanged) and kenyon (light only: Kenyon purple header bar and links, serif headings, no horizontal overflow at 390 px). Store settings as key/value rows (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL); accept only a theme folder that exists. When no theme is stored, use CMS_THEME (default classic) and add CMS_THEME=classic to .env.example. Saving the theme is a site update through update_site, so a failed deploy refuses the change. The console preview's /style.css serves the selected theme. Guard /admin/settings with require_admin and show the Settings link only inside the admin block of templates/admin/_nav.html.`\n- Then `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`; walk the checklist at 1280 and 390 px.\n- Push + PR: `git push -u origin mp2plus-theme`, `gh pr create --title \"MP2plus P1: Switchable theme\" --body \"Closes #N\"`.\n- Review: `/code-review`, then `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on pull request #<pr>, then commit and push the fixes to this branch.` At least one commit pushed after the comment.\n- Commit prefix: `T<N>:`\n- Merge: `gh pr merge <pr> --merge --delete-branch`; `git switch main && git pull`; `gh issue view N` shows CLOSED by the PR.\n- Screenshots: home page in kenyon, `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `-390.png`.\n- Report rows: `| F8 | issue #N; tests/test_theme.py; mp2plus-theme-1280.png, mp2plus-theme-390.png |` and\n  `| P1 | PR #<pr> closing issue #N; carries F8 |`\n\n### 3. P3 Decision record\n- Phase: `echo P3 > .claude/state/phase`\n- Issue/branch: none; on `main`.\n- Prompt: none needed; the table and ADR-006 draft exist. Reword the \"why\"s in your own voice if you like,\n  check ADR-006 against the S2 code, and set its status to accepted.\n- Review: read both against the code (P3 row 6).\n- Commit: `P3: ...` with CONTEXT.md, ADR-006 and this file; push.\n- Report row: `| P3 | CONTEXT.md Decisions table; docs/adr/ADR-006-login-limiter-in-memory.md |`\n\n### 4. S1 Access matrix\n- Phase: `echo S1 > .claude/state/phase`\n- Issue/branch: none; on `main`.\n- Prompt (`/clear` first): the manual's S1 prompt, plus:\n  `Seed demo content in the test and fill {item_id} with a real page's id and {account_id} with the editor's id. For the anonymous client use follow_redirects=False and assert a 302, 303 or 307 whose Location path is /login. Send a valid session CSRF token on every POST, so the editor's 403 can only come from require_admin.`\n- Check: add a throwaway `require_admin` route, rerun `uv run pytest -q tests/test_access_matrix.py`, see it covered, delete it.\n- Review: `/code-review`; fix findings.\n- Commit: `S1: ...`, push.\n- Report row: `| S1 | tests/test_access_matrix.py |`\n\n### Then Part 2\nReport `docs/iphs400_mp2plus-web-cms_report_rafael-frias_<YYYYMMDD>.md` with the rows above, the two checks,\n`git tag mp2plus-final && git push origin mp2plus-final`, email.\n\"\"\"The site update: render published content into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nrender_site() writes the home page (the Travel Lineup page if published, then\npublished posts newest first), one file per published post under posts/ and\none per published page under pages/. Every page carries a nav built from the\npublished pages. The console previews the same pages at / through home_html()\nand item_html(), so it shows what readers will see.\n\nupdate_site() is what the console runs for any change to published content\n(ADR-004): the change, the render and the deploy succeed or fail together.\n`cms publish` calls render_site() and `cms deploy` the default deployer, so\nthe Webmaster can still do either step by hand.\n\nTwo rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom sqlite3 import Connection\nfrom typing import TypeVar\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content, db, settings\nfrom app.content import Item, Kind, Status\nfrom app.deploy import Deployer, DeployFailed\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Phones first: one column, nothing wider than the screen. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem;\n       padding: 1rem; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nheader .console { float: right; font-weight: 400; }\nnav ul { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; gap: 0.25rem 1rem; list-style: none;\n         margin: 0.5rem 0 0; padding: 0; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\nimg, table, pre { max-width: 100%; }\n/* Wide tables and code scroll in their own box, not the page. */\ntable, pre { display: block; overflow-x: auto; }\n.byline { color: GrayText; font-size: 0.9rem; }\n.lineup { border-bottom: 1px solid GrayText; margin-bottom: 1.5rem; }\n/* The console shares this file: form fields never run off a phone. */\ntextarea, input, select { max-width: 100%; box-sizing: border-box; }\ntextarea { width: 100%; }\nnav form { display: inline; }\n[role=\"status\"] { border-left: 4px solid GrayText; padding-left: 0.5rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\nTRAVEL_LINEUP = \"travel-lineup\"\n\n\ndef byline(email: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The author's name on the public site: the part of the email before @.\n\n    The full email is never published, so readers can't harvest it (ADR-005).\n    \"\"\"\n    return email.split(\"@\", 1)[0]\n\n\ndef reader_date(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An ISO UTC timestamp as readers see it, 'Oct 14, 2026', in the team\n    laptop's time zone, so an evening post isn't dated tomorrow.\"\"\"\n    return datetime.fromisoformat(timestamp).astimezone().strftime(\"%b %d, %Y\")\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    env = Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n    env.filters[\"byline\"] = byline\n    env.filters[\"reader_date\"] = reader_date\n    return env\n\n\ndef published(source: db.Source, kind: Kind) -> list[Item]:\n    \"\"\"Newest first. A database that doesn't exist yet (a fresh clone) has none.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(source, Path) and not source.exists():\n        return []\n    return content.list_items(source, kind, Status.PUBLISHED)\n\n\ndef _render(template: str, prefix: str, nav_pages: list[Item], preview: bool,\n            **context) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Render a public page that sits `prefix` (\"\" or \"../\") below the root.\n\n    Every link is built from `prefix`, so the paths stay relative. The nav\n    lists pages oldest first, in the order the Coach created them.\n    \"\"\"\n    nav_pages = sorted(nav_pages, key=lambda p: (p.created_at, p.id))\n    return environment().get_template(template).render(\n        title=settings.SITE_TITLE, prefix=prefix, nav_pages=nav_pages,\n        css_path=f\"{prefix}style.css\", home_path=f\"{prefix}index.html\",\n        console_path=f\"{prefix}admin\" if preview else None, **context,\n    )\n\n\ndef home_html(pages: list[Item], posts: list[Item], preview: bool = False) -> str:\n    \"\"\"index.html: the Travel Lineup (if published), then posts newest first.\n\n    A preview (the console's /) also links to the console; site/ never does.\n    \"\"\"\n    lineup = next((p for p in pages if p.slug == TRAVEL_LINEUP), None)\n    return _render(\n        \"public/home.html\", \"\", pages, preview, posts=posts, lineup=lineup,\n        lineup_body=render_markdown(lineup.body) if lineup else None,\n    )\n\n\ndef item_html(item: Item, pages: list[Item], preview: bool = False) -> str:\n    \"\"\"posts/<slug>.html or pages/<slug>.html, its Markdown sanitized.\"\"\"\n    return _render(\"public/item.html\", \"../\", pages, preview, item=item,\n                   body=render_markdown(item.body))\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None,\n                source: db.Source | None = None) -> Path:\n    \"\"\"Rebuild `out` from scratch with every published item in `source`.\"\"\"\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    source = source or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    pages = published(source, Kind.PAGE)\n    posts = published(source, Kind.POST)\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    for kind in Kind:\n        (out / f\"{kind}s\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(home_html(pages, posts))\n    for item in pages + posts:\n        (out / f\"{item.kind}s\" / f\"{item.slug}.html\").write_text(\n            item_html(item, pages))\n    return out\n\n\nT = TypeVar(\"T\")\n\n\nclass SiteUpdateFailed(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The site update failed, so the change it was for was rolled back.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef update_site(db_path: Path, out: Path, deploy: Deployer,\n                change: Callable[[Connection], T]) -> T:\n    \"\"\"Make `change` to published content and put the result on the website.\n\n    The change is staged in one transaction, `out` is rendered from that\n    would-be state, and `deploy` sends it. Only after a successful deploy is\n    the change committed. If anything fails, the change is rolled back and\n    `out` is rendered again from what is saved, so it matches the website. On one\n    team laptop, that is accepted.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n            result = change(conn)\n            render_site(out, conn)\n            deploy(out)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        render_site(out, db_path)\n        if isinstance(exc, DeployFailed):\n            raise SiteUpdateFailed(str(exc)) from exc\n        raise\n    return result\n\"\"\"The SQLite database: one file, opened per operation.\n\nThe database is never committed (it is gitignored); scripts/seed_demo.py\nrebuilds it on a fresh clone.\n\nFunctions that read or write take a `Source`: usually the database's path,\nbut a site update passes an open connection instead, so a change and the\nsite rendered from it share one transaction (see publish.update_site()).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (active IN (0, 1))\n);\n\n-- Posts and pages share one table; kind drives navigation and permissions.\n-- Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC strings, so they sort as text.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    kind       TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('post', 'page')),\n    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    body       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'\n                       CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts (id),\n    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\nSource = Path | sqlite3.Connection\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect(source: Source) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open the database, commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\n\n    Given an open connection, use it as is: whoever opened it commits or\n    rolls back, so the changes made here stay staged until then.\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(source, sqlite3.Connection):\n        yield source\n        return\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(source)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the tables if they do not exist yet.\"\"\"\n    with connect(path) as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\n\n`.env` at the repo root is read first, so `cp .env.example .env` followed by\n`uv run cms serve` works with no sourcing step. CMS_ENV_FILE names a different file, or \"\"\nfor none (the tests use that, so a developer's .env never reaches them).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef load_env_file(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Copy KEY=value lines from `path` into os.environ, unless already set.\n\n    Understands blank lines, # comments, an `export ` prefix and values in\n    single or double quotes, which is all .env.example uses.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.is_file():\n        return\n    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():\n        line = line.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \"=\" not in line:\n            continue\n        key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n        key = key.removeprefix(\"export \").strip()\n        if not key:\n            continue\n        value = value.strip()\n        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in \"\\\"'\":\n            value = value[1:-1]\n        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)\n\n\n_env_file = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ENV_FILE\", str(ROOT / \".env\"))\nif _env_file:\n    load_env_file(Path(_env_file))\n\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\")\n# \"on\" only on the team laptop: every site update then pushes to gh-pages, and\n# a failed push blocks the change (ADR-004). A fresh clone leaves it unset, so\n# publishing there only renders site/ and never pushes to someone else's repo.\nDEPLOY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_DEPLOY\", \"\").lower() == \"on\"\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n\"\"\"The deployer: sends the rendered site/ to the web host (ADR-004).\n\nA deployer is any callable that takes the site directory and raises if the\nsite did not reach the host. create_app() takes one; tests pass a fake. The\ndefault is push_to_gh_pages() (which `cms deploy` also uses) when CMS_DEPLOY\nis \"on\", and render_only() otherwise, so a fresh clone never pushes.\n\nGitHub access comes from the environment, never from a committed file. When\nCMS_GITHUB_TOKEN is set, git sends it as an HTTP header (through git's\nGIT_CONFIG_* variables, so it never appears in a command line). Without it,\ngit uses whatever credentials the team laptop already has. The token is read\nhere at each deploy, not in settings.py at start-up, so one set later is used.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport base64\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nDeployer = Callable[[Path], None]\n\n# Long enough for a slow hotel network, short enough that a request never hangs.\nTIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120\n\n\nclass DeployFailed(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The site did not reach the host (no network, or GitHub said no).\"\"\"\n\n\ndef render_only(site: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Send nothing: the site update stops at site/ (CMS_DEPLOY is not on).\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _git_env() -> dict[str, str]:\n    env = os.environ | {\"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT\": \"0\"}\n    token = os.environ.get(\"CMS_GITHUB_TOKEN\", \"\")\n    if token:\n        basic = base64.b64encode(f\"x-access-token:{token}\".encode()).decode()\n        env |= {\"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", message,\n             str(site)],\n            cwd=settings.ROOT, env=_git_env(), capture_output=True, text=True,\n            timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom datetime import datetime\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom sqlite3 import Connection\nfrom typing import TypeVar\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import content, db, settings\nfrom app.content import Item, Kind, Status\nfrom app.deploy import Deployer, DeployFailed\nfrom app.markdown import render_markdown\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Phones first: one column, nothing wider than the screen. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; On one\n    team laptop, that is accepted.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        with db.connect(db_path) as conn:\n            result = change(conn)\n            render_site(out, conn)\n            deploy(out)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        render_site(out, db_path)\n        if isinstance(exc, DeployFailed):\n            raise SiteUpdateFailed(str(exc)) from exc\n        raise\n    return result\n\"\"\"The SQLite database: one file, opened per operation.\n\nThe database is never committed (it is gitignored); scripts/seed_demo.py\nrebuilds it on a fresh clone.\n\nFunctions that read or write take a `Source`: usually the database's path,\nbut a site update passes an open connection instead, so a change and the\nsite rendered from it share one transaction (see publish.update_site()).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nSCHEMA = \"\"\"\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (\n    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    email         TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,\n    password_hash TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    role          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (role IN ('admin', 'editor')),\n    active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1 CHECK (active IN (0, 1))\n);\n\n-- Posts and pages share one table; kind drives navigation and permissions.\n-- Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC strings, so they sort as text.\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS items (\n    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,\n    kind       TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('post', 'page')),\n    title      TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    slug       TEXT    NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    body       TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',\n    status     TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT 'draft'\n                       CHECK (status IN ('draft', 'published')),\n    author_id  INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts (id),\n    created_at TEXT    NOT NULL,\n    updated_at TEXT    NOT NULL\n);\n\"\"\"\n\n\nSource = Path | sqlite3.Connection\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef connect(source: Source) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:\n    \"\"\"Open the database, commit on success, roll back on error, always close.\n\n    Given an open connection, use it as is: whoever opened it commits or\n    rolls back, so the changes made here stay staged until then.\n    \"\"\"\n    if isinstance(source, sqlite3.Connection):\n        yield source\n        return\n    conn = sqlite3.connect(source)\n    conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n    conn.execute(\"PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON\")\n    try:\n        with conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        conn.close()\n\n\ndef init(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Create the tables if they do not exist yet.\"\"\"\n    with connect(path) as conn:\n        conn.executescript(SCHEMA)\n\"\"\"Configuration, read from the environment (never hard-code secrets).\n\n`.env` at the repo root is read first, so `cp .env.example .env` followed by\n`uv run cms serve` works with no sourcing step. Variables already set in the\nenvironment win over the file. CMS_ENV_FILE names a different file, or \"\"\nfor none (the tests use that, so a developer's .env never reaches them).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]\n\n\ndef load_env_file(path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Copy KEY=value lines from `path` into os.environ, unless already set.\n\n    Understands blank lines, # comments, an `export ` prefix and values in\n    single or double quotes, which is all .env.example uses.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.is_file():\n        return\n    for line in path.read_text().splitlines():\n        line = line.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\") or \"=\" not in line:\n            continue\n        key, value = line.split(\"=\", 1)\n        key = key.removeprefix(\"export \").strip()\n        if not key:\n            continue\n        value = value.strip()\n        if len(value) >= 2 and value[0] == value[-1] and value[0] in \"\\\"'\":\n            value = value[1:-1]\n        os.environ.setdefault(key, value)\n\n\n_env_file = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ENV_FILE\", str(ROOT / \".env\"))\nif _env_file:\n    load_env_file(Path(_env_file))\n\nTEMPLATES = ROOT / \"templates\"\nSITE = ROOT / \"site\"\n\nSECRET_KEY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SECRET_KEY\", \"dev-only-not-for-production\")\nDATABASE_PATH = Path(os.environ.get(\"CMS_DATABASE\", ROOT / \"cms.db\"))\nSITE_TITLE = os.environ.get(\"CMS_SITE_TITLE\", \"Kenyon Men's Golf CMS\")\n# \"on\" only on the team laptop: every site update then pushes to gh-pages, and\n# a failed push blocks the change (ADR-004). A fresh clone leaves it unset, so\n# publishing there only renders site/ and never pushes to someone else's repo.\nDEPLOY = os.environ.get(\"CMS_DEPLOY\", \"\").lower() == \"on\"\n# Set this to your Pages URL once you deploy, e.g.\n# https://yourname.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/\nBASE_PATH = os.environ.get(\"CMS_BASE_PATH\", \"\")\n\"\"\"The deployer: sends the rendered site/ to the web host (ADR-004).\n\nA deployer is any callable that takes the site directory and raises if the\nsite did not reach the host. create_app() takes one; tests pass a fake. The\ndefault is push_to_gh_pages() (which `cms deploy` also uses) when CMS_DEPLOY\nis \"on\", and render_only() otherwise, so a fresh clone never pushes.\n\nGitHub access comes from the environment, never from a committed file. When\nCMS_GITHUB_TOKEN is set, git sends it as an HTTP header (through git's\nGIT_CONFIG_* variables, so it never appears in a command line). Without it,\ngit uses whatever credentials the team laptop already has. The token is read\nhere at each deploy, not in settings.py at start-up, so one set later is used.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport base64\nimport os\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nDeployer = Callable[[Path], None]\n\n# Long enough for a slow hotel network, short enough that a request never hangs.\nTIMEOUT_SECONDS = 120\n\n\nclass DeployFailed(Exception):\n    \"\"\"The site did not reach the host (no network, or GitHub said no).\"\"\"\n\n\ndef render_only(site: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Send nothing: the site update stops at site/ (CMS_DEPLOY is not on).\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _git_env() -> dict[str, str]:\n    env = os.environ | {\"GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT\": \"0\"}\n    token = os.environ.get(\"CMS_GITHUB_TOKEN\", \"\")\n    if token:\n        basic = base64.b64encode(f\"x-access-token:{token}\".encode()).decode()\n        env |= {\"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"http.https://github.com/.extraheader\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": f\"AUTHORIZATION: basic {basic}\"}\n    return env\n\n\ndef push_to_gh_pages(site: Path, message: str = \"Site update\") -> None:\n    \"\"\"Commit `site` to the gh-pages branch and push it to origin.\"\"\"\n    try:\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", message,\n             str(site)],\n            cwd=settings.ROOT, env=_git_env(), capture_output=True, text=True,\n            timeout=TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n        )\n    except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:\n        raise DeployFailed(str(exc)) from exc\n    if result.returncode != 0:\n        raise DeployFailed(result.stderr.strip() or \"git push failed\")","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"serverClassifierContext":{"request":"1b67d056-bc4d-4cec-b34d-7bd5c1ceb3ef","context":{"git_state":{"cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","root":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","branch":"mp2plus-theme","default_branch":null,"status":{"clean":false,"counts":{"staged":0,"modified":2,"untracked":null,"untracked_normal":7},"porcelain":null,"truncated":false},"visibility":{"origin":{"host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"},"push_remote":"origin","remotes":[{"name":"origin","host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}],"visibility_cache":[{"host":"github.com","remote":"RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms","visibility":"public"}]}},"live_cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","platform":"wsl"}},"sandboxed":false,"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2e733b58-1e51-4de1-8cdc-8f2481353a36","permissionDecision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reasonType":"classifier"},"session_id":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9594e59a-8f80-44aa-92ae-9c2ec172e923","version":"2.1.307","gitBranch":"mp2plus-theme"}

cat templates/admin/_nav.html templates/admin/accounts.html templates/base.html","description":"Read web app, routes, templates"}},"wireIngestContext":{"toolu_01Dk5HkxgiCqc9rYC8QjxaHX":{"cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"001c0147-8fc4-46b2-a548-79fbbc4b6de3","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CgGSnpog6WbFAc83W8vZB","requestRef":"da4d9c75-4403-436d-9ef0-37b09304b91b","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"95d9fddc-f80a-4155-8dca-058e3dcc6c98","timestamp":"2026-10-22T01:57:01.986Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9594e59a-8f80-44aa-92ae-9c2ec172e923","version":"2.1.307","gitBranch":"mp2plus-theme"}
{"parentUuid":"95d9fddc-f80a-4155-8dca-058e3dcc6c98","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"92ae58e9-7ced-4365-9141-12901d3e03f9","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Dk5HkxgiCqc9rYC8QjxaHX","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"What every console route shares: templates, CSRF, and who is logged in.\n\nThree dependencies do the guarding:\n\n  - `verify_csrf` goes on every state-changing (POST) route. It rejects the\n    request with 403 unless the form's csrf_token matches the session's.\n  - `current_account` goes on every console route (the console router in\n    app/routes/console.py applies it to all of them). Someone who isn't\n    logged in, or whose account was deactivated, is sent to /login.\n  - `require_admin` goes on admin-only routes. It does what `current_account`\n    does, then refuses editors with 403, so a typed URL is denied, not just\n    a hidden link.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hmac\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, settings\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `current_account`; create_app() turns it into a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use. Put it in every form.\"\"\"\n    if \"csrf\" not in request.session:\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return request.session[\"csrf\"]\n\n\ndef root(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The relative path from this page back to the site root (\"\", \"../\", ...).\n\n    Console links are written as {{ root(request) }}admin/accounts, so they stay\n    relative yet still work when a form re-renders a page at a deeper URL such\n    as /admin/accounts/5/role.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"../\" * (request.url.path.count(\"/\") - 1)\n\n\ndef when(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An ISO UTC timestamp as the console shows it: '2026-10-14 18:05 UTC'.\"\"\"\n    return f\"{timestamp[:16].replace('T', ' ')} UTC\"\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\ntemplates.env.globals[\"root\"] = root\ntemplates.env.filters[\"when\"] = when\n\n\ndef verify_csrf(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(\"\")) -> None:\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not (expected and hmac.compare_digest(expected, csrf_token)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account:\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = (accounts.get_account(request.app.state.db_path, account_id)\n               if account_id is not None else None)\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.clear()\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return account\n\n\ndef require_admin(account: Account = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n    if not account.is_admin:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Only admins can do that.\")\n    return account\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin and needs a login (/login); a preview\nof the public site answers at /. Routes live in their own modules under\napp/routes/ and are included here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, deploy, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, items, public\nfrom app.web import LoginRequired\n\n\ndef create_app(db_path: Path | None = None,\n               site_dir: Path | None = None,\n               deployer: deploy.Deployer | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.state.db_path = db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    # Where site updates write; tests pass a temporary directory.\n    app.state.site_dir = site_dir or settings.SITE\n    # Sends each site update to the web host; tests pass a fake (ADR-004).\n    app.state.deployer = deployer or (\n        deploy.push_to_gh_pages if settings.DEPLOY else deploy.render_only)\n    db.init(app.state.db_path)\n\n    # Signed session cookie that ends when the browser closes (shared laptop).\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(items.posts_router)\n    app.include_router(items.pages_router)\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The admin console's home: a dashboard, and one content list for everything.\n\nEvery route on this router requires a logged-in account. The dashboard counts\nposts and pages by status. The content list shows posts and pages together,\nnewest updated first, with one filter bar (status, then kind, then author);\nthe filters combine. /admin/posts and /admin/pages show the same list with\nthe kind already chosen (app/routes/items.py).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom enum import StrEnum\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\n\nfrom app import accounts, content\nfrom app.accounts import Account\nfrom app.content import Kind, Status\nfrom app.web import current_account, templates\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin\", dependencies=[Depends(current_account)])\n\n\nclass NoMatch(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A filter value that matches no item, e.g. ?status=archived.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _choice[E: StrEnum](enum: type[E], value: str) -> E | None:\n    \"\"\"'' means any; an unknown value matches nothing rather than failing.\"\"\"\n    if not value:\n        return None\n    try:\n        return enum(value)\n    except ValueError:\n        raise NoMatch(value) from None\n\n\ndef _author(value: str) -> int | None:\n    if not value:\n        return None\n    if not (value.isascii() and value.isdecimal()):\n        raise NoMatch(value)\n    return int(value)\n\n\ndef content_list(request: Request, me: Account, *, status: str = \"\",\n                 kind: str = \"\", author: str = \"\"):\n    \"\"\"The content list, filtered by whatever the filter bar sent.\"\"\"\n    db_path = request.app.state.db_path\n    try:\n        items = content.find_items(db_path, _choice(Kind, kind),\n                                   _choice(Status, status), _author(author))\n    except NoMatch:\n        items = []\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/content.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Content\", \"account\": me, \"items\": items,\n         \"can_change\": content.can_change,\n         \"statuses\": list(Status), \"kinds\": list(Kind),\n         \"authors\": accounts.list_accounts(db_path),\n         \"chosen\": {\"status\": status, \"kind\": kind, \"author\": author}},\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef dashboard(request: Request, account: Account = Depends(current_account)):\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/dashboard.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Dashboard\", \"account\": account, \"kinds\": list(Kind),\n         \"statuses\": list(Status),\n         \"counts\": content.count_items(request.app.state.db_path)},\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"/content\")\ndef all_content(request: Request, me: Account = Depends(current_account),\n                status: str = \"\", kind: str = \"\", author: str = \"\"):\n    return content_list(request, me, status=status, kind=kind, author=author)\n\"\"\"A preview of the public site at /, for whoever is at the team laptop.\n\nThe pages come from the same code that writes site/ (app/publish.py), so the\nCoach sees exactly what readers will see once the site update has run. route shares: templates, CSRF, and who is logged in.\n\nThree dependencies do the guarding:\n\n  - `verify_csrf` goes on every state-changing (POST) route. It rejects the\n    request with 403 unless the form's csrf_token matches the session's.\n  - `current_account` goes on every console route (the console router in\n    app/routes/console.py applies it to all of them). Someone who isn't\n    logged in, or whose account was deactivated, is sent to /login.\n  - `require_admin` goes on admin-only routes. It does what `current_account`\n    does, then refuses editors with 403, so a typed URL is denied, not just\n    a hidden link.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport hmac\nimport secrets\n\nfrom fastapi import Depends, Form, HTTPException, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import accounts, settings\nfrom app.accounts import Account\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\nclass LoginRequired(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised by `current_account`; create_app() turns it into a redirect.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef csrf_token(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The session's CSRF token, created on first use. Put it in every form.\"\"\"\n    if \"csrf\" not in request.session:\n        request.session[\"csrf\"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n    return request.session[\"csrf\"]\n\n\ndef root(request: Request) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The relative path from this page back to the site root (\"\", \"../\", ...).\n\n    Console links are written as {{ root(request) }}admin/accounts, so they stay\n    relative yet still work when a form re-renders a page at a deeper URL such\n    as /admin/accounts/5/role.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"../\" * (request.url.path.count(\"/\") - 1)\n\n\ndef when(timestamp: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"An ISO UTC timestamp as the console shows it: '2026-10-14 18:05 UTC'.\"\"\"\n    return f\"{timestamp[:16].replace('T', ' ')} UTC\"\n\n\ntemplates.env.globals[\"csrf_token\"] = csrf_token\ntemplates.env.globals[\"root\"] = root\ntemplates.env.filters[\"when\"] = when\n\n\ndef verify_csrf(request: Request, csrf_token: str = Form(\"\")) -> None:\n    expected = request.session.get(\"csrf\", \"\")\n    if not (expected and hmac.compare_digest(expected, csrf_token)):\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Invalid or missing CSRF token.\")\n\n\ndef current_account(request: Request) -> Account:\n    account_id = request.session.get(\"account_id\")\n    account = (accounts.get_account(request.app.state.db_path, account_id)\n               if account_id is not None else None)\n    if account is None or not account.active:\n        request.session.clear()\n        raise LoginRequired\n    return account\n\n\ndef require_admin(account: Account = Depends(current_account)) -> Account:\n    if not account.is_admin:\n        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail=\"Only admins can do that.\")\n    return account\n\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nThe admin console lives under /admin and needs a login (/login); a preview\nof the public site answers at /. Routes live in their own modules under\napp/routes/ and are included here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\nfrom starlette.middleware.sessions import SessionMiddleware\n\nfrom app import db, deploy, settings\nfrom app.routes import accounts, auth, console, items, public\nfrom app.web import LoginRequired\n\n\ndef create_app(db_path: Path | None = None,\n               site_dir: Path | None = None,\n               deployer: deploy.Deployer | None = None) -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n    app.state.db_path = db_path or settings.DATABASE_PATH\n    # Where site updates write; tests pass a temporary directory.\n    app.state.site_dir = site_dir or settings.SITE\n    # Sends each site update to the web host; tests pass a fake (ADR-004).\n    app.state.deployer = deployer or (\n        deploy.push_to_gh_pages if settings.DEPLOY else deploy.render_only)\n    db.init(app.state.db_path)\n\n    # Signed session cookie that ends when the browser closes (shared laptop).\n    app.add_middleware(SessionMiddleware, secret_key=settings.SECRET_KEY,\n                       session_cookie=\"cms_session\", max_age=None,\n                       same_site=\"lax\")\n\n    @app.exception_handler(LoginRequired)\n    def to_login(request: Request, exc: LoginRequired):\n        return RedirectResponse(\"/login\", status_code=303)\n\n    app.include_router(auth.router)\n    app.include_router(console.router)\n    app.include_router(accounts.router)\n    app.include_router(items.posts_router)\n    app.include_router(items.pages_router)\n    app.include_router(public.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"The admin console's home: a dashboard, and one content list for everything.\n\nEvery route on this router requires a logged-in account. The dashboard counts\nposts and pages by status. with\nthe kind already chosen (app/routes/items.py).\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom enum import StrEnum\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Request\n\nfrom app import None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        try:\n            push_to_gh_pages(settings.SITE, args.message)\n        except DeployFailed as exc:\n            print(f\"Deploy failed: {exc}\")\n            return 1\n        print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n              \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return 0\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise {"parentUuid":"02c2af4d-30ef-47c1-8d82-31b171ad4199","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b0b83e4d-9d5b-4da0-805d-d3c778d566f2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"<command-message>mattpocock-skills:implement</command-message>\n<command-name>/mattpocock-skills:implement</command-name>\n<command-args>#10 Switchable theme, CSS only. Follow the issue's acceptance checklist exactly. Move the CSS out of app/publish.py into app/themes/<name>/style.css and add a second theme. The theme is chosen on an admin-only Settings page at /admin/settings, stored in a settings table; build that page if it does not exist yet. cms publish writes the selected theme's CSS as site/style.css. Check both themes at 390 px wide. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Put the new tests in tests/test_theme.py and name each one test_step<k>_<what> after the acceptance step it checks. Ask before adding any dependency. The two themes are classic (today's CSS, moved unchanged) and kenyon (light only: Kenyon purple header bar and links, serif headings, no horizontal overflow at 390 px). Store settings as key/value rows (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL); accept only a theme folder that exists. When no theme is stored, use CMS_THEME (default classic) and add CMS_THEME=classic to .env.example. Saving the theme is a site update through update_site, so a failed deploy refuses the change. The console preview's /style.css serves the selected theme. Guard /admin/settings with require_admin and show the Settings link only inside the admin block of templates/admin/_nav.html. We are on branch mp2plus-theme; commit messages start \"T10:\". {"parentUuid":"c46250a0-2020-4a00-be6d-f3230f159f0a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgGSyfVPk3cpWfr8Fe35L","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_012Jw13XXnvytvdhjeXavcoV","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/tests/test_theme.py","content":"\"\"\"F8 (#10): the Coach switches the public site's theme on the Settings page.\n\nEach test is named after the acceptance step it checks:\n\n  1. Two themes exist, each one CSS file in its own folder under app/themes/.\n  2. The admin Settings page selects the theme, and the choice survives a\n     server restart.\n  3. Publishing writes the selected theme's CSS as site/style.css, so every\n     page's relative stylesheet link still works.\n  4. Switching back and publishing again restores the first theme's CSS.\n  5. Both themes show no horizontal overflow at 390 px (walked by hand; here\n     only the phone-first rules each stylesheet must carry).\n  6. The Settings form carries a CSRF token; its POST without it is refused.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\n\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app import settings, theme\nfrom app.main import create_app\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\nTHEMES_DIR = settings.ROOT / \"app\" / \"themes\"\n\n\ndef choose(post_form, c: TestClient, name: str):\n    return post_form(c, \"/admin/settings\", theme=name)\n\n\ndef selected_on_page(c: TestClient) -> str:\n    match = re.search(r'value=\"(\\w+)\" checked', c.get(\"/admin/settings\").text)\n    assert match, \"No theme is checked on the Settings page\"\n    return match.group(1)\n\n\ndef theme_css(name: str) -> str:\n    return (THEMES_DIR / name / \"style.css\").read_text()\n\n\n# --- step 1: two themes, one CSS file each ------------------------------------\n\ndef test_step1_two_themes_each_one_css_file_in_its_own_folder():\n    assert theme.available() == [\"classic\", \"kenyon\"]\n    for name in theme.available():\n        files = [f.name for f in (THEMES_DIR / name).iterdir()]\n        assert files == [\"style.css\"], (name, files)\n\n\ndef test_step1_kenyon_is_light_with_purple_and_serif_headings():\n    css = theme_css(\"kenyon\")\n    assert \"color-scheme: light;\" in css and \"dark\" not in css\n    assert \"--kenyon-purple\" in css and \"serif\" in css\n\n\n# --- step 2: the Settings page selects the theme, and it lasts ----------------\n\ndef test_step2_settings_page_defaults_to_classic(client_as):\n    assert selected_on_page(client_as(\"admin\")) == \"classic\"\n\n\ndef test_step2_admin_selects_a_theme_that_survives_a_restart(\n        client_as, post_form, db_path, site_dir, deployer):\n    admin = client_as(\"admin\")\n    response = choose(post_form, admin, \"kenyon\")\n    assert response.status_code == 303\n    assert selected_on_page(admin) == \"kenyon\"\n\n    restarted = TestClient(create_app(db_path=db_path, site_dir=site_dir,\n                                      deployer=deployer))\n    assert restarted.get(\"/style.css\").text == theme_css(\"kenyon\")\n\n\ndef test_step2_the_console_preview_serves_the_selected_theme(\n        client_as, post_form, client):\n    assert client.get(\"/style.css\").text == theme_css(\"classic\")\n    choose(post_form, client_as(\"admin\"), \"kenyon\")\n    response = client.get(\"/style.css\")\n    assert response.text == theme_css(\"kenyon\")\n    assert {"parentUuid":"6ad50e8a-bdbe-4a01-a524-6d77b52f70bd","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgGT23qN3xU631gHW5xFM","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01936Fs7hb7f14PfBkmRppFx","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms/app/theme.py","content":"\"\"\"The public site's theme: one stylesheet, chosen on the Settings page.\n\nEach theme is a folder under app/themes/ holding one style.css. The Coach's\nchoice is the 'theme' row of the settings table (key/value rows). Until one\nis stored, CMS_THEME decides (default classic). Only a folder that exists is\never used, so a typo or a path never reaches the published site.\n\nA site update renders site/style.css from the theme its transaction sees, so\nsaving a theme goes through publish.update_site() like any published change.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom app import db, settings\n\nTHEMES = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / \"themes\"\nDEFAULT = \"classic\"\nKEY = \"theme\"\n\n\nclass UnknownTheme(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"No folder under app/themes/ has that name.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef available() -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Theme names, sorted: each folder under app/themes/ with a style.css.\"\"\"\n    return sorted(p.parent.name for p in THEMES.glob(\"*/style.css\"))\n\n\ndef selected(source: db.Source) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The stored theme, else CMS_THEME, else classic; always one that exists.\"\"\"\n    for name in (_stored(source), settings.THEME):\n        if name in available():\n            return name\n    return DEFAULT\n\n\ndef css(source: db.Source) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The selected theme's stylesheet, as site/style.css carries it.\"\"\"\n    return (THEMES / selected(source) / \"style.css\").read_text()\n\n\ndef set_theme(source: db.Source, name: str) -> None:\n    if name not in available():\n        raise UnknownTheme(name)\n    with db.connect(source) as conn:\n        conn.execute(\n            \"INSERT INTO settings (key, value) VALUES (?, ?) \"\n            \"ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = excluded.value\",\n            (KEY, name))\n\n\ndef _stored(source: db.Source) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"None for a fresh clone (no database) or one made before settings existed.\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(source, Path) and not Editors get 403 on every route here.\n\nThe Coach chooses the site-wide options, starting with the theme. Saving a\ntheme is a site update (ADR-004): the public site is rebuilt in the new\ntheme and deployed, and if the deploy fails the choice is not saved.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Depends, Form, Request\nfrom fastapi.responses import RedirectResponse\n\nfrom app import publish, theme\nfrom app.accounts import Account\nfrom app.routes.items import OFFLINE\nfrom app.web import require_admin, templates, verify_csrf\n\nrouter = APIRouter(prefix=\"/admin/settings\", dependencies=[Depends(require_admin)])\n\nSAVED = \"Theme saved and the website updated.\"\n\n\ndef _page(request: Request, me: Account, *, chosen: str | None = None,\n          error: str = \"\", saved: str = \"\", status_code: int = 200):\n    db_path = request.app.state.db_path\n    return templates.TemplateResponse(\n        request, \"admin/settings.html\",\n        {\"title\": \"Settings\", \"account\": me, \"themes\": theme.available(),\n         \"chosen\": chosen or theme.selected(db_path),\n         \"error\": error, \"saved\": saved},\n        status_code=status_code,\n    )\n\n\n@router.get(\"\")\ndef settings_page(request: Request, me: Account = Depends(require_admin)):\n    return _page(request, me, saved=request.session.pop(\"settings_saved\", \"\"))\n\n\n@router.post(\"\", dependencies=[Depends(verify_csrf)])\ndef save_settings(request: Request, me: Account = Depends(require_admin),\n                  name: str = Form(\"\", alias=\"theme\")):\n    if name not in theme.available():\n        return _page(request, me, error=\"Choose one of the themes.\",\n                     status_code=400)\n    state = request.app.state\n    try:\n        publish.update_site(state.db_path, state.site_dir, state.deployer,\n                            lambda conn: theme.set_theme(conn, name))\n    except publish.SiteUpdateFailed:\n        return _page(request, me, chosen=name, error=OFFLINE, status_code=503)\n    request.session[\"settings_saved\"] = SAVED\n    return RedirectResponse(\"/admin/settings\", {"type":"api-request-blob","sessionId":"9594e59a-8f80-44aa-92ae-9c2ec172e923","hash":"3c22b7a60bdf29dd458c9dad81030f5ea8aa7225f05f6455cede43c94376d09d","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_019wYs7isu8AWLjY8g6RHJdB","content":"Launching skill: mattpocock-skills:code-review"},{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). {"parentUuid":"a7ac277f-dc31-4fc7-aebe-d28b18dcbf35","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"b0b83e4d-9d5b-4da0-805d-d3c778d566f2","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/refiv/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/code-review\n\nTwo-axis review of the diff between `HEAD` and a fixed point the user supplies:\n\n- **Standards**: does the code conform to this repo's documented coding standards?\n- **Spec**: does the code faithfully implement the originating issue / spec?\n\nBoth axes run as **parallel sub-agents** so they don't pollute each other's context, then this skill aggregates their findings.\n\nThe issue tracker should have been provided to you. If `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md` is missing, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n### 1. Pin the fixed point\n\nWhatever the user said is the fixed point (a commit SHA, branch name, tag, `main`, `HEAD~5`, etc.). If they didn't specify one, ask for it.\n\nCapture the diff command once: `git diff <fixed-point>...HEAD` (three-dot, so the comparison is against the merge-base). Also note the list of commits via `git log <fixed-point>..HEAD --oneline`.\n\nBefore going further, confirm the fixed point resolves (`git rev-parse <fixed-point>`) and the diff is non-empty. A bad ref or empty diff should fail here, not inside two parallel sub-agents.\n\n### 2. Identify the spec source\n\nLook for the originating spec, in this order:\n\n1. Issue references in the commit messages (`#123`, `Closes #45`, GitLab `!67`, etc.), fetched via the workflow in `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.\n2. A path the user passed as an argument.\n3. A spec file under `docs/`, `specs/`, or `.scratch/` matching the branch name or feature.\n4. If nothing is found, ask the user where the spec is. If they say there isn't one, the **Spec** sub-agent will skip and report \"no spec available\".\n\n### 3. Identify the standards sources\n\nAnything in the repo that documents how code should be written, such as `CODING_STANDARDS.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`.\n\nOn top of whatever the repo documents, the Standards axis always carries the **smell baseline** below: a fixed set of Fowler code smells (_Refactoring_, ch.3) that applies even when a repo documents nothing. Two rules bind it:\n\n- **The repo overrides.** A documented repo standard always wins; where it endorses something the baseline would flag, suppress the smell.\n- **Always a judgement call.** Each smell is a labelled heuristic (\"possible Feature Envy\"), never a hard violation. Like any standard here, skip anything tooling already enforces.\n\nEach smell reads *what it is* → *how to fix*; match it against the diff:\n\n- **Mysterious Name**: a function, variable, or type whose name doesn't reveal what it does or holds. → rename it; if no honest name comes, the design's murky.\n- **Duplicated Code**: the same logic shape appears in more than one hunk or file in the change. → extract the shared shape, call it from both.\n- **Feature Envy**: a method that reaches into another object's data more than its own. → move the method onto the data it envies.\n- **Data Clumps**: the same few fields or params keep travelling together (a type wanting to be born). → bundle them into one type, pass that.\n- **Primitive Obsession**: a primitive or string standing in for a domain concept that deserves its own type. → give the concept its own small type.\n- **Repeated Switches**: the same `switch`/`if`-cascade on the same type recurs across the change. → replace with polymorphism, or one map both sites share.\n- **Shotgun Surgery**: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files in the diff. → gather what changes together into one module.\n- **Divergent Change**: one file or module is edited for several unrelated reasons. → split so each module changes for one reason.\n- **Speculative Generality**: abstraction, parameters, or hooks added for needs the spec doesn't have. → delete it; inline back until a real need shows.\n- **Message Chains**: long `a.b().c().d()` navigation the caller shouldn't depend on. → hide the walk behind one method on the first object.\n- **Middle Man**: a class or function that mostly just delegates onward. → cut it, call the real target direct.\n- **Refused Bequest**: a subclass or implementer that ignores or overrides most of what it inherits. → drop the inheritance, use composition.\n\n### 4. Spawn both sub-agents in parallel\n\n**Standards sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The full diff command and commit list.\n- The list of standards-source files you found in step 3, **plus the smell baseline from step 3** pasted in full (the sub-agent has no other access to it).\n- The brief: \"Report, per file/hunk where relevant, (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard: cite the standard (file + the rule); and (b) any baseline smell you spot: name it and quote the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls: documented-standard breaches can be hard, but baseline smells are always judgement calls, and a documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Skip anything tooling enforces. Under 400 words.\"\n\n**Spec sub-agent prompt** should include:\n\n- The diff command and commit list.\n- The path or fetched contents of the spec.\n- The brief: \"Report: (a) requirements the spec asked for that are missing or partial; (b) behaviour in the diff that wasn't asked for (scope creep); (c) requirements that look implemented but where the implementation looks wrong. Quote the spec line for each finding. Under 400 words.\"\n\nIf the spec is missing, skip the Spec sub-agent and note this in the final report.\n\n### 5. Aggregate\n\nPresent the two reports under `## Standards` and `## Spec` headings, verbatim or lightly cleaned. Do **not** merge or rerank findings, because the two axes are deliberately separate (see _Why two axes_).\n\nEnd with a one-line summary: total findings per axis, and the worst issue _within each axis_ (if any). Don't pick a single winner across axes: that's the reranking the separation exists to prevent.\n\n## Why two axes\n\nA change can pass one axis and fail the other:\n\n- Code that follows every standard but implements the wrong thing → **Standards pass, Spec fail.**\n- Code that does exactly what the issue asked but breaks the project's conventions → **Spec pass, Standards fail.**\n\nReporting them separately stops one axis from masking the other.\n\n\nARGUMENTS: Uncommitted working-tree changes since HEAD (e6fb8ea) on branch mp2plus-theme, limited to F8 files: app/theme.py, app/themes/, app/db.py, app/settings.py, app/publish.py, app/main.py, app/routes/public.py, app/routes/settings_page.py, templates/admin/_nav.html, templates/admin/settings.html, .env.example, tests/test_theme.py. Ignore CONTEXT.md, notes/, docs/.\n\nSpec:\n1. GitHub issue #10 acceptance checklist:\n| 1 | Two themes exist, each one CSS file in its own folder under `app/themes/` | read |\n| 2 | The admin Settings page selects the theme, and the choice survives a server restart | walk, test |\n| 3 | `uv run cms publish` writes the selected theme's CSS as `site/style.css`, so every page's relative stylesheet link still works | publish, test |\n| 4 | Switching back and publishing again restores the first theme's CSS | publish, test |\n| 5 | Both themes show no horizontal overflow at 390 px on the home page and one post | walk |\n| 6 | The Settings form carries a CSRF token; its POST replayed without the token is refused | replay, test |\n2. The user's instructions: Move the CSS out of app/publish.py into app/themes/<name>/style.css. Settings page at /admin/settings, admin-only, stored in a settings table. cms publish writes the selected theme's CSS as site/style.css. No href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. Schema change: keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example. Existing tests may only gain cases. New tests in tests/test_theme.py named test_step<k>_<what>. No new dependencies. Themes: classic (today's CSS, moved unchanged) and kenyon (light only: Kenyon purple header bar and links, serif headings, no horizontal overflow at 390 px). Settings as key/value rows (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL); accept only a theme folder that exists. The change goes through `publish.update_site`, a failed deploy returns 503 with the `OFFLINE` message, and the choice is rolled back.\n  - **CONTEXT.md vocabulary:** used correctly (Coach, Theme, Settings page, site update).\n  - **Docstring convention (judgement):** every public function in `theme.py` and the sibling modules has a one-line docstring, but `theme.set_theme` (theme.py:45) has none.\n  - **Formatting (judgement):** the rewrapped module docstring in `publish.py:3-4` now breaks after \"the home page (the Travel Lineup page if published, then\" and leaves a ragged short line.\n  \n  **(b) Baseline smells (all judgement calls).**\n  - **Duplicated Code: the default theme name.** \"classic\" is hard-coded in three places: `theme.DEFAULT = \"classic\"`, `settings.THEME = os.environ.get(\"CMS_THEME\", \"classic\")` and `.env.example`. `settings.THEME` could default to `theme.DEFAULT`, or the other way round.\n  - **Duplicated Code: theme validation.** It runs twice. The route checks `if name not in theme.available(): ... status_code=400`, and `set_theme` also does `raise UnknownTheme(name)`. The route never catches `UnknownTheme`, so the exception class is close to Speculative Generality. Either catch `theme.UnknownTheme` in the route or drop the pre-check.\n  - **Shotgun Surgery / misplaced shared constant.** `from app.routes.items import OFFLINE` makes one route module depend on another route module. `OFFLINE` is the general \"site update failed\" message and belongs beside `SiteUpdateFailed` or in `app/web.py`.\n  - **Duplicated Code: the two stylesheets.** `classic/style.css` and `kenyon/style.css` repeat the whole phone-first block (`img, table, pre {max-width:100%}`, `overflow-x:auto`, the textarea rules, the nav rules). The spec asks for one CSS file per theme and test step 5 pins the duplication, so the repo standard overrides this. Note only that a layout fix now has to be made in both files.\n  - **Primitive Obsession (minor).** A theme name is a bare `str` checked against `available()`, which globs the filesystem on every call. `selected()` can call it twice per `/style.css` request. This is acceptable at this scale.\n  - **Mysterious Name (minor).** `theme.KEY = \"theme\"` is vague; `SETTINGS_KEY` would say what it is. The module name `settings_page` is fine as a way to avoid clashing with `app.settings`.\n  \n  No blockers. The two items most worth fixing are the missing docstring on `set_theme` and the `OFFLINE` import from `app.routes.items`.\n</agent-message>"}

The message text is unchanged |\n| Mysterious name `theme.KEY` | **Fixed**: renamed `SETTINGS_KEY` |\n| Theme validated twice (route pre-check + `UnknownTheme` in `set_theme`) | **Kept on purpose**: the route returns a 400 before any site update starts, so a bad name never triggers a render. `set_theme` keeps the \"only an existing folder\" rule at the data layer for any other caller |\n| \"classic\" default appears in `theme.DEFAULT`, `settings.THEME` and `.env.example` | **Kept**: `settings` can't import `theme` (`theme` imports `settings`), and `.env.example` must spell the value out. `theme.selected()` still falls back to `DEFAULT` for an unknown `CMS_THEME` |\n| The two stylesheets repeat the phone-first rules | **Kept**: the spec asks for one self-contained CSS file per theme, and `test_step5` pins the shared rules in both |\n| `available()` globs the filesystem on every call | **Kept**: two folders, one console user; fine at this scale |\n\n### Spec: nothing missing or wrong\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| Row 5 (no overflow at 390 px) can only be checked by walking it | **Walked**: home page and one post rendered in both themes inside a 390 px frame in headless Chromium: `clientWidth=390 scrollWidth=390` in all four cases, so no horizontal overflow. The test checks the phone-first rules each stylesheet must carry |\n| `seed_demo.py` from `.env.example` not yet run | **Done**: ran clean against a fresh database with `.env.example` values |\n| Kenyon adds small touches (footer colour, rounded header, purple lineup and status borders) | **Kept**: within \"Kenyon purple header bar and links, serif headings\"; layout rules unchanged |\n| An unknown `CMS_THEME` falls back to classic | **Kept**: follows \"accept only a theme folder that exists\" |\n\nChecks: `uv run pytest -q` gives 236 passed (219 before + 17 in `tests/test_theme.py`); `uv run python scripts/check_submission.py --stage 2` gives 22/22.\nEOF\ngh issue comment 10 -R RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms -F $S/review.md","description":"Post review findings on issue 10"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}]}}

{"parentUuid":"a7aaa178-ca07-43d6-bd16-44920005b7b0","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CgGTzQXNwN4GqbAY6uq1d","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"#10 is built and committed on `mp2plus-theme` as `c89a98e`, with \"Closes #10\" in the message. It is not pushed. Every check passes: 236 tests (the 219 from before plus 17 new ones in `tests/test_theme.py`) and `check_submission.py --stage 2` at 22/22.\n\n**You need to run this**, because I added a `settings` table to the database:\n```\nrm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n```\nI already ran the seed script against a fresh database using the `.env.example` values, and it ran clean. An old `cms.db` without the new table still works for publishing (it just falls back to `CMS_THEME`), and the console creates the table when it starts.\n\n**Acceptance checklist:**\n1. **Two themes:** `app/themes/classic/style.css` is byte-for-byte the CSS that was in `publish.py`. `app/themes/kenyon/style.css` is light only, with a purple header bar and links and serif headings.\n2. **Settings page:** `/admin/settings` is admin-only (`require_admin`). The choice is stored as the `('theme', name)` row and lasts after a server restart. Only an existing theme folder is accepted; anything else gets a 400. Saving goes through `update_site`, so if the deploy fails you get a 503 and the old theme stays. With no stored theme, `CMS_THEME` is used, and `CMS_THEME=classic` is now in `.env.example`. The Settings link appears only in the admin block of the console nav.\n3. **Publishing** writes the selected theme as `site/style.css`, and the stylesheet links stay relative. The console preview's `/style.css` also serves the selected theme.\n4. **Switching back** to classic and publishing again restores the classic CSS.\n5. **390 px:** I loaded the home page and one post in both themes inside a 390 px frame in the headless Chromium already in Playwright's cache, so no new dependency. All four came out 390 px wide with nothing overflowing. The automated test for this step can only check that each stylesheet carries the phone-sized layout rules, so the real check is the measurement.\n6. **CSRF:** the form carries the token. A POST with no token or a forged one gets a 403 and triggers no site update.\n\n**Review:** both reviews found no hard violations and no missing requirements. I fixed four small points, the main one being that the \"website not updated\" message now lives in `app/publish.py` instead of being imported from another route. I kept four other points on purpose. All of it, with reasons, is posted on the issue: https://github.com/RafaelFrias1/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/10#issuecomment-6331024356\n\n**Left out of the commit:**\n- `CONTEXT.md`, ADR-006 and `notes/mp2plus-grill-decisions.md` stay uncommitted for P3, as you asked.\n- `notes/usage-ledger.csv` and the five transcripts in `docs/transcripts/` are also uncommitted. CLAUDE.md says transcripts go in every commit, but you said to stage only F8 files.\n- Two existing test files, `test_t07` and `test_t08`, weren't touched.\n- The repo has no type checker set up, so none was run.\n\nYour grill notes list the next steps as the walk at 1280 and 390 px, the screenshots, and then the push and PR."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1020,"cache_read_input_tokens":107823,"output_tokens":1135,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":26},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1020,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"global","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1135,"cache_read_input_tokens":107823,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1020,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1020},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"624ac9d4-cd9a-40b2-9159-3e66eef33316","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011CgGTzPy8fdumTcxjkr6Jq","requestRef":"41b2d1e3-39ab-407f-9fee-f4fa87a6cdf0","requestedModel":"claude-opus-5-5","type":"assistant","uuid":"1928929a-5766-428e-bba5-552d7999b014","timestamp":"2026-10-22T02:12:54.813Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"medium","perTurnEffort":"medium","session_id":"e68901dd-4f60-40d0-873c-0a5584ccf73d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/refiv/ubuncode/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9594e59a-8f80-44aa-92ae-9c2ec172e923","version":"2.1.307","gitBranch":"mp2plus-theme"}
