{"parentUuid":"b4f9b114-d18b-4da3-b921-72ef00f41b0f","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"a64e61b5-68ca-4529-ae60-d2495e43d473","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WFjFXik9d3m6HuyNcaS8Pu","type":"tool_result","content":"#### F8 Switchable theme (7 pts, about 35–50 min)\n- **Goal.** Your client changes the site's look without a developer. Two themes, each one CSS file, are selectable on the admin Settings page, and `cms publish` exports the selected one.\n- **Prerequisites.** MP2 done and Part 0 complete. Shares the Settings page with F7 (see F7). The template keeps its CSS as a string in `app/publish.py`; this exercise moves it into a theme file.\n- **Roles.** The Settings page: admin only.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. Create the issue (runbook 1), title `MP2plus F8: Switchable theme`; then `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase`.\n2. `/clear`, then the prompt below with your issue number. Then `rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py`, then walk the acceptance checklist yourself; fix what fails.\n3. `/code-review`, then the close-out message (runbook 5). `gh issue view <issue#>` shows CLOSED, with your comment above the close.\n4. Save `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-theme-1280.png` and `mp2plus-theme-390.png`: the home page in the second theme. Then run the two checks (runbook 8).\n\n#### P1 Pull-request workflow (6 pts, about 30–45 min)\n- **Goal.** Ship one change through a branch, a pull request and a review before the merge, the way most teams work.\n- **Prerequisites.** Part 0 complete. P1 carries one change: a feature from this menu (scored as that feature too), or one item from your MP2 feedback's repair list, written as a small issue. A repair earns P1's points only, not MP2 points.\n- **Roles.** No new routes of its own; a carried feature keeps its own Roles line.\n\n**Steps.**\n1. Create the issue first. For a feature, that feature's step 1. For a repair: `gh issue create --label stretch --title \"MP2plus P1: <the repair>\"`, body = two to four acceptance steps, then `Blocked by: none`. Set the phase: `echo T<issue#> > .claude/state/phase` for a feature, `echo P1 > .claude/state/phase` for a repair.\n2. Branch: `git switch main && git pull && git switch -c mp2plus-<slug>`.\n3. `/clear`, then the feature's prompt or the prompt below; let it commit on the branch.\n4. `git push -u origin mp2plus-<slug>`, then `gh pr create --title \"MP2plus P1: <the change>\" --body \"Closes #<issue#>\"`.\n5. `/code-review`, then: `Post the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on pull request #<pr#>, then commit and push the fixes to this branch.`\n6. `gh pr merge <pr#> --merge --delete-branch`, then `git switch main && git pull` and `gh issue view <issue#>`. **Expected:** CLOSED, closed by your pull request, with the review comment on the PR dated before the merge.\n\n**Prompt.** For a repair (a feature uses its own prompt):\n```text\n/implement #N <the repair, in one sentence>. Follow the issue's acceptance steps exactly. Rules: no href=\"/ or src=\"/ in any template, admin pages included; use url_for or relative links. Every new form carries a CSRF token and refuses a POST without it. Every new setting gets a line in .env.example. If you change the database schema, keep scripts/seed_demo.py running clean from .env.example and tell me to run rm cms.db && uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py. Tests that existed before may only gain cases; ask me before changing an existing assertion. Ask before adding any dependency.\n```\n**Acceptance checklist.**\n| # | Step | Checked by | Pts |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | The issue's `createdAt` is before the branch's first push | github | 1 |\n| 2 | The PR comes from a branch off `main`, and its body contains `Closes #<issue#>` | github | 1 |\n| 3 | A `/code-review` findings comment on the PR, listing each finding and how it was resolved, is dated before `mergedAt` | github | 2 |\n| 4 | At least one commit was pushed to the branch after that comment | github | 1 |\n| 5 | The PR is merged, and the merge closed the issue | github | 1 |\n\n- **Out of scope.** Reviews by another person, protected branches, CI.\n- **Deliverables.** The closed issue; the merged PR; your report row.\n- **Report row.** `| P1 | PR #<n> closing issue #<n>; carries <F-id, or \"MP2 repair: <what>\"> |`\n- **Scoring.** One point per row as listed. Total 6. When P1 carries a feature, row 3's comment is also that feature's findings comment (its Trail line); a missing or late comment costs both.\n\n### 2. How scoring works\n- **Points only, no levels.** Each exercise scores its own points. The sum is capped at +30 and added to the MP2 score; the result may exceed 100 and is recorded as is. There is no pass line.\n- **The report rows say what is scored.** Every exercise with a row in the report is scored; an exercise without a row is not, and the feedback names it. The plan does not limit what counts. Over +30, the judge scores all, applies the cap, and reports the rest.\n- **Only the range counts.** Work in `mp2plus-base..mp2plus-final` is scored. A feature already present at `mp2plus-base` is not scored again. Commits of a merged MP2 resubmission named in the report are MP2 work and are not scored.\n- **The gate comes first.** If P0.3 or P0.4 fails, every exercise scores 0 until a resubmission fixes it.\n- **A feature worth P points** scores four lines:\n  - **Screenshots, 1:** `docs/screenshots/mp2plus-{slug}-1280.png` and `-390.png` both present.\n  - **Trail, 1:** the issue's `createdAt` is before the first push of the feature's first commit, AND a `/code-review` findings comment on the issue (or its closing PR) is dated before the issue's `closedAt`. {"parentUuid":"7373f78a-f1f8-4b5b-aff7-e2b7590c2310","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"c63e1195-6bfe-47ef-88ba-9166a64f02a4","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01Q7Ldawn7ErTQcEg3j9ws5K","type":"tool_result","content":"Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.\nDeleted branch mp2plus-theme (was a4b7bd2).\n00aeff2 Merge pull request #11 from RafaelFrias1/mp2plus-theme\na4b7bd2 T10: home page screenshots in the kenyon theme (1280 and 390 px)\nc89a98e T10: switchable theme, chosen on the admin Settings page\n0\n## Decisions\n\n| Question | Choice | Why |\n|---|---|---|\n| What does the login limiter count by? | The typed email, including emails with no account, not the IP address | All posting happens on one team laptop, so an IP limit would lock out the Coach whenever someone else on it mistyped; and counting unknown emails too means the 429 can't tell anyone which emails have accounts (checklist #2). |\n| Where are failed logins remembered? | In the server's memory; a restart clears them | The console runs as one process on the one team laptop, so a single in-memory count sees every login attempt; a table would mean a schema change and an rm cms.db reseed on that laptop, and losing the count on restart only helps someone who can already restart the laptop. |\n| When does a new theme reach the public site? | Immediately, as a site update; no wifi means the change is refused | The Coach doesn't want to learn new software mid-season; if he picks a theme and the public site doesn't change until someone next publishes a post, he'll think it's broken. Same rule as ADR-004: a change is live or it isn't saved. |\n# ADR-006: The login limiter keeps failed logins in memory\n\n**Status:** accepted (S2, commit 9aa5eef)\n**Date:** 2026-10-21\n\n## Context\n\nChecklist #2 and MP2plus S2: after 5 failed logins for one email within 15\nminutes, the next attempt is refused with 429, even with the right password.\nThe count has to live somewhere. The console runs as one process on the one\nteam laptop (`cms serve`), and the schema in `app/db.py` is only ever created,\nnever migrated: a new table means `rm cms.db` and a reseed on that laptop.\nOptions considered: a `failed_logins` table in `cms.db`, a limiter on\n`app.state` (one per app), and one limiter object in its own module.\n\n## Decision\n\nOne module-level limiter holds, per typed email (trimmed, lowercased), the\ntimes of its recent failed logins. It reads the time through a `clock`\nattribute (`time.monotonic` by default), so tests can freeze and advance it.\nA successful login clears that email's failures. The autouse fixture\n`reset_limiter` in `tests/conftest.py` clears it and restores the real clock\nbefore every test.\n\nRejected: a `failed_logins` table, which survives restarts but costs a schema\nchange and a reseed, and is already reset by each test's fresh database;\nand `app.state`, because the `login_as` fixture builds a new app per client,\nso failures would not carry from one client to the next.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- No schema change and no reseed for S2.\n- Restarting the console clears every lockout. Only someone who can already\n  restart the team laptop gains from that; accepted.\n- Running more than one server process would split the count. On one laptop\n  there is one process; moving off it means revisiting this ADR.\n- Tests share one limiter, so the autouse fixture is what keeps the 212\n  existing tests from tripping a 429.\n- The check, the password verify and the recording of a failure run under a\n  per-email lock (one of 64, chosen by hashing the email), so simultaneous\n  guesses cannot get past the 5-try limit. Unrelated emails that share a lock\n  wait behind each other's argon2 verify; with the console never public and\n  one team on the laptop, accepted.\n- The lockout message gives the minutes left, rounded up. It reveals nothing,\n  because unknown emails lock out the same way.\n- Nothing lifts a lockout early: it ends on its own (`CONTEXT.md`, Lockout).\n# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack.
